feature: Interactive Human Player Agent for FAB Games
workflow_rationale: New component (HumanAgent class + runner script) added to existing rl_agents/ module. No existing code changes needed; the new agent plugs into the existing engine agent interface.

phases.name: HumanAgent Class
phases.description: Create the HumanAgent class with game state display, human-readable action formatting, input validation, and the callable agent interface. This is the core interactive component.

subtasks.description: Create HumanAgent class in rl_agents/human_agent.py implementing the full interactive agent interface. Must include: (1) __call__(state, options, context) conforming to agent protocol, (2) _display_state() showing both players' health, human's hand with card details (name, cost, power, defense, pitch), equipment status, combat state, resources, action points, turn number, game step, (3) _format_action() producing human-readable action descriptions for all 17 ActionTypes (e.g., 'Play Wounding Blow [cost:2, power:6, pitch: card_a]' instead of raw repr), (4) _format_action_list() displaying numbered options grouped by type for long lists, (5) Input validation with re-prompting on non-numeric, out-of-range, or empty input, (6) Auto-select when only one legal action, (7) Non-Action option display and selection (start-player choice, trigger ordering), (8) Ctrl+C handling with clean 'Game aborted' message, (9) Hidden info enforcement (only show human's hand/arsenal, opponent's public info only).

verification.command: python -c "from rl_agents.human_agent import HumanAgent; agent = HumanAgent(player_id=1); print('HumanAgent created OK')"

phases.name: CLI Runner Script
phases.description: Create the play_vs_iql.py CLI runner that sets up and executes human-vs-bot games with support for multiple opponent types, deck selection, and seat choice.

subtasks.description: Create rl_agents/play_vs_iql.py CLI runner script with: (1) argparse CLI with --checkpoint, --deck (default to first available deck), --seat (1 or 2), --opponent (iql|heuristic|random), --list-decks, --max-turns, --device, --embedder-bundle, --seed flags, (2) Deck resolution: search DECKS_DIR and DECKS_DIR/generated/ for deck files, support --list-decks to show available decks, (3) Opponent instantiation: IQLPolicyAgent (from evaluate_iql_vs_random.py) for 'iql', HeuristicBot for 'heuristic', RandomAgent for 'random', (4) IQL checkpoint + embedder bundle loading following evaluate_iql_vs_random.py pattern, (5) GameRunRequest setup with deck paths, agents, CardDB, seeds, max_turns, (6) Game execution via build_game_backend('local').run_game(req), (7) End-of-game summary: winner, turns played, final HP of both players, (8) Entry point: python -m rl_agents.play_vs_iql, (9) Top-level KeyboardInterrupt handling for clean abort.

phases.name: Testing & Package Exports
phases.description: Update package exports, create unit tests for HumanAgent, and verify no regressions in existing test suite.

subtasks.description: Update rl_agents/__init__.py to export HumanAgent. Create tests/test_human_agent.py with unit tests covering: (1) HumanAgent handles Action options with mocked stdin input, (2) HumanAgent handles non-Action options (strings, ints) with mocked input, (3) HumanAgent auto-selects when only one option exists (no input prompt), (4) HumanAgent returns empty/non-list options directly, (5) _display_state() produces output without errors for various GameState configurations (action phase, combat phase, empty hand, etc.), (6) _format_action() returns readable strings for all major ActionType values (PASS, PLAY_CARD, ATTACK_WEAPON, DEFEND_CARDS, DEFEND_EQUIPMENT, STORE_ARSENAL, etc.), (7) Input validation: non-numeric input causes re-prompt (use mock), out-of-range index causes re-prompt. Use unittest.mock.patch('builtins.input') for simulating user input. Use real GameState objects from conftest.py fixtures where available, or construct minimal mock states.
subtasks.notes: Exported HumanAgent from rl_agents/__init__.py. Created tests/test_human_agent.py with 27 passing tests covering all required scenarios.

subtasks.description: Run the full existing test suite to verify no regressions. All pre-existing tests must continue to pass with the new files added.

parallelism.speedup_estimate: No parallel speedup - single-service sequential dependency chain

acceptance_criteria: All existing tests pass (python -m pytest tests/ -x)
HumanAgent can be imported and instantiated
No modifications to engine/ or existing agent source files

verification_steps.name: CLI Help Verification
verification_steps.expected_outcome: Usage info printed with all expected arguments

verification_strategy.reasoning: Low risk feature adding new files only. Unit tests verify HumanAgent logic with mocked input. Manual play-testing validates the interactive experience.
